claims.claim: BAE Systems identifies Terrier as a British Army combat engineer vehicle designed for mobility support, counter-mobility and survivability engineering tasks.
claims.evidence: BAE Systems states that Terrier entered British Army service and lists obstacle and route clearance, anti-tank ditch and obstacle construction, and trench or AFV-slot digging among its typical applications.

claims.claim: Terrier can be remotely controlled at distances up to 1 km and can be configured with mine-plough and investigation-arm equipment for route proving and clearance.
claims.evidence: BAE Systems reports wireless remote control to 1 km and separately describes field-trialled mine-plough and long-reach investigation-arm capabilities for mine and IED route clearance.

candidates.notes: Candidate only; later canonicalization should distinguish baseline Terrier capability from later optional or trialled attachments.

candidates.proposed_title: WiSENT 2 multifunctional support and engineering vehicle

claims.claim: FFG describes WiSENT 2 as a modular Leopard 2-based support platform configurable for recovery, engineering, mine-clearing and bridge-laying roles.
claims.evidence: The manufacturer product page explicitly states that WiSENT 2 is based on the Leopard 2 chassis and can be configured in recovery, engineering, mine-clearing or bridge-laying roles.

claims.claim: The WiSENT 2 AEV combines an articulated excavator and engineer blade, while mine-clearing configuration can add a full-width mine plough, lane-marking system and magnetic-signature duplicator.
claims.evidence: FFG lists the articulated excavator and pioneer clearing blade for the AEV role and separately lists the full-width mine plough, lane-marking system and magnetic-signature duplicator for mine-clearing configuration.

candidates.notes: Preserve role-specific configuration boundaries if later appended; not every WiSENT 2 carries every engineering kit simultaneously.

claims.claim: The U.S. Army ODIN database identifies the M1150 Assault Breacher Vehicle as an M1 Abrams-chassis mine- and explosives-clearing vehicle.
claims.evidence: The U.S. Army OE Data Integration Network describes the M1150 ABV as based on the M1 Abrams chassis and purpose-built to clear pathways through minefields, roadside bombs and improvised explosive devices.

claims.claim: The M1150 ABV combines a front-mounted mine plough with explosive line-charge capability for obstacle and minefield breaching.
claims.evidence: ODIN explicitly lists a mine plough and line charges as defining equipment of the M1150 Assault Breacher Vehicle.

candidates.notes: Candidate uses the current U.S. Army ODIN description for identity and capability; historical combat-use claims are not required for canonicalization.
